RULES.currentRule: Georgia requires photo ID to vote in person: driver's license, state ID, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal ID, or a free Voter ID card issued by the county registrar. Absentee ballot applications and return envelopes require an ID number (driver's license/state ID number or last four digits of SSN), per SB 202 (2021).
RULES.whyItMatters: GA-10 voters across all 20 counties (12 whole + 8 partial) must present qualifying photo ID at the polls, and absentee voters must provide an ID number on both their application and return envelope. Voters lacking ID can obtain a free Voter ID card from their county registrar.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: full current-cycle citation to the Georgia SOS voter-ID page was not independently re-fetched this research pass; verify exact accepted-ID list against sos.ga.gov before publishing.

RULES.currentRule: Absentee ballot requests open approximately 78 days before Election Day and must be submitted no later than 11 days before Election Day (Oct. 23, 2026 for the Nov. 3 general). Still governed by SB 202 (2021), the Election Integrity Act.
RULES.whyItMatters: GA-10 voters who want to vote absentee must plan around a shorter request window than existed before 2021 — missing the 11-day cutoff means voting in person is the only remaining option.
RULES.detail: SB 202 (2021), the Election Integrity Act. NEEDS REVIEW: exact hour-of-day cutoff for the 11-day request deadline not independently re-confirmed against a live SOS calendar document.

RULES.currentRule: SB 202 (2021) restricts absentee ballot drop boxes to indoor locations at county election offices or early-voting sites, with reduced availability compared to 2020. Drop boxes are capped at roughly one per 100,000 registered voters (or one per site) in each county. GA-10 voters should check the My Voter Page (mvp.sos.ga.gov) for county-approved drop box locations.
RULES.whyItMatters: GA-10's mostly rural counties (Elbert, Franklin, Hart, Taliaferro, Wilkes, and others) may have zero or one drop box, typically inside the county elections office and available only during early-voting hours. Athens-Clarke, Oconee, Barrow, Walton, and Gwinnett (Dacula-area only) have confirmed drop boxes; several smaller GA-10 counties remain unverified.
RULES.detail: SB 202 (2021). Drop-box availability could not be independently confirmed for Elbert, Franklin, Hart, Taliaferro, or Wilkes counties in the July 2026 research pass.

RULES.currentRule: Under SB 202, ballots cast at the wrong precinct on Election Day are not counted for precinct-specific races. Provisional ballots cast at the wrong precinct after 5:00 p.m. may be counted only for races the voter was otherwise eligible to vote in (e.g., federal and statewide races), not local down-ballot races tied to the correct precinct.
RULES.whyItMatters: GA-10 voters who show up at the wrong precinct on Election Day risk having some or all of their ballot rejected. This is especially important in the district's split counties (Gwinnett, Hancock, Henry, Jasper, Newton, Putnam, Taliaferro, Wilkes) where neighboring precincts may fall in a different congressional district. Voters should confirm their correct polling location via My Voter Page before Election Day.
RULES.detail: SB 202 (2021), Election Integrity Act. Especially consequential in GA-10 due to the district's 8 partial counties.

RULES.topic: Ballot tabulation method for Nov 3, 2026 (SB 189 ban delayed by SB 3EX)
RULES.currentRule: For the November 3, 2026 general election, Georgia will continue using its existing touchscreen ballot-marking devices that produce QR-coded paper ballots, with QR-code tabulation. This resolves the pre-July uncertainty: SB 189 (2024) had banned QR-code tabulation effective July 1, 2026, but SB 3EX — passed during the 2026 special session and signed by Gov. Brian Kemp on June 25, 2026 — delayed that ban to Jan 1, 2028. SB 3EX also creates an Election Equipment Specifications and Standards Committee (report due Jan 31, 2027) to recommend a replacement system, and mandates automatic hand recounts for the top two statewide races on the ballot decided by less than 0.5% (does not apply to U.S. House races such as GA-10). Every GA-10 county will therefore use the same tabulation approach as prior cycles.
RULES.whyItMatters: Resolves what had been the largest pre-election uncertainty for GA-10 voters. Every GA-10 county will run the same ballot-marking and counting process as 2022 and 2024 (touchscreen ballot-marking devices producing QR-coded paper ballots). Note that the automatic-hand-recount provision from SB 3EX can affect same-ballot statewide races (e.g., the concurrent U.S. Senate general and the governor's race) if margins fall below 0.5%, which could delay overall ballot certification.
RULES.detail: SB 189 (2024) ban delayed to Jan 1, 2028 by SB 3EX (signed June 25, 2026). GA-10 counties use touchscreen BMDs with QR-code tabulation for Nov 3, 2026. SB 3EX also adds an automatic hand-recount trigger (<0.5%) for top-2 statewide races — not applicable to the GA-10 U.S. House race but applicable to same-ballot statewide contests.

RULES.currentRule: Georgia requires a runoff election if no candidate in a general-election race receives more than 50% of the vote. If triggered, the runoff is held approximately four weeks later. For the 2026 general election, the runoff date is December 1, 2026, with abbreviated early voting Nov 23-25 (Thanksgiving week).
RULES.whyItMatters: Not expected to apply in GA-10's U.S. House race given the clean two-candidate field (Gaines vs. DeLancy), which produces a majority winner in the first count. Still relevant context for GA-10 voters following the concurrent U.S. Senate general (Collins vs. Ossoff), which could plausibly go to a runoff.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: exact statutory citation and hour-of-day cutoffs not independently re-confirmed this pass.

RULES.currentRule: County boards of elections must certify by 5 PM on the Monday following Election Day (Nov 9, 2026 for the Nov 3 general), per O.C.G.A. §§ 21-2-493(k) and 21-2-497. The Secretary of State must certify statewide results by 5 PM on the 17th day following the election (Nov 20, 2026), per O.C.G.A. § 21-2-499(b).
RULES.whyItMatters: GA-10 voters concerned about post-election litigation or contested results should be aware of these firm deadlines. County-level certification refusals in 2024 prompted litigation; the certification duty is ministerial (non-discretionary) under Georgia law.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: state certification date (Nov 20) computed from statute — differs from a commonly assumed Nov 17 date; cross-check against SOS's published 2026 calendar.

RULES.topic: Congressional map stability for 2026 (2023 court-ordered plan)
RULES.currentRule: GA-10 is administered under the 2023 court-ordered congressional map (adopted after the 2021 map was found to dilute Black voting power in the Atlanta area). In the 2023 redraw, GA-10 lost Jackson County to GA-09 and gained Franklin and Hart counties from GA-09. The Georgia legislature considered redrawing maps in a June 2026 special session but dropped those plans, leaving GA-10 unchanged for 2026.
RULES.whyItMatters: GA-10 voters can rely on the same district boundaries used in the 2024 election. No pending litigation was identified that threatens GA-10's map for the 2026 cycle. Voters in newly-added Franklin and Hart counties (added in 2023) should confirm their congressional district assignment via My Voter Page.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: the specific enacted-plan PDF for the 2023 court-ordered congressional map should be independently re-fetched from legis.ga.gov and archived before publication.

CONFLICTS.factInQuestion: Statewide ballot-tabulation method for the November 3, 2026 general election.
CONFLICTS.sourceAClaim: SB 189 (2024) prohibits QR-code-based ballot tabulation effective July 1, 2026. Secretary of State guidance interprets this as compatible with continued touchscreen-machine use if the 'official' tabulation is derived from OCR of the ballot images rather than the QR codes.
CONFLICTS.sourceBClaim: State Election Board's June 4, 2026 non-binding resolution (3-1) permits counties to switch to hand-marked paper ballots if the legislature fails to fund a replacement system, contradicting the SOS interpretation.
CONFLICTS.whyItMatters: Every GA-10 county's Election Day process depends on which interpretation controls. Voters and poll workers may see materially different ballot-marking and counting procedures depending on their county's chosen approach — and adjacent counties in GA-10 could plausibly go different directions.
CONFLICTS.suggestedReviewAction: RESOLVED 2026-07-20: SB 3EX, signed by Gov. Kemp on June 25, 2026 during the special session, delays the SB 189 QR-code tabulation ban from July 1, 2026 to Jan 1, 2028. Georgia will continue using its existing touchscreen ballot-marking devices with QR-code tabulation for Nov 3, 2026 in all GA-10 counties. Both the SOS interpretation and the SEB hand-marked-paper option are moot for this cycle — the pre-existing tabulation system remains in place. See rule-ga-sb189-ballot-tabulation for the current authoritative rule, and news-ga10-00gbvmx (Mountain Country Radio, 2026-07-15) plus src-ballotpedia-sb3ex (2026-06-29) for corroboration.

CONFLICTS.factInQuestion: State (SOS) certification deadline for the November 3, 2026 general.
CONFLICTS.sourceAClaim: O.C.G.A. § 21-2-499(b) requires certification by 5 PM on the 17th day following the election — Nov 20, 2026 for a Nov 3 election.
CONFLICTS.sourceBClaim: Commonly cited references (including NCSL summaries and prior-cycle deadline lists) reference a Nov 17 certification deadline, which is not consistent with a strict '17th day following' reading of statute.
CONFLICTS.whyItMatters: A 3-day difference matters for post-election litigation timelines, contested-race procedures, and voter expectations around results finality.
CONFLICTS.suggestedReviewAction: Confirm against the Secretary of State's officially published 2026 election calendar (PDF) once released.

Directly contradicts the Secretary of State's guidance to keep touchscreen machines with OCR post-processing.

NEWS.headline: Georgia election board adopts new rules targeting election mistrust
NEWS.relevanceSummary: SEB adopted two new rules: (1) prohibiting tabulation from an electronic copy of a ballot rather than the paper original, and (2) requiring all vote tabulation/consolidation to be in public view of election monitors. AG Chris Carr warned one rule could invite constitutional challenge. Affects every GA-10 county's Nov 3 procedure.

NEWS.headline: State Election Board sends complaint against Oconee County to Attorney General
NEWS.relevanceSummary: GA-10-specific: SEB voted 3-0 (Johnson, Grubbs, King in favor) to refer to the Georgia AG a complaint that Oconee County's 2020 and 2022 candidate-qualifying periods were held at the wrong time under state law. Live, unresolved administrative matter affecting a whole GA-10 county.

NEWS.headline: Only five days of early voting for Oconee's June 16 runoff

Worth flagging as a capacity-planning question for Nov 3.

NEWS.headline: Georgia election board adopts new rules targeting election mistrust
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The State Election Board adopted new statewide rules requiring that vote tabulation occur directly from paper ballots rather than electronic copies and that all tabulations and consolidations happen in public, changing how every Georgia county administers counts and transparency procedures.[1]

WEEKLY_REPORT.summary: Initial build for GA-10 (cloned from the GA-02 dashboard template) followed by same-day resolution of the SB 189 tabulation-method conflict via SB 3EX. Open-seat race after Mike Collins (R, inc.) vacated to run for U.S. Senate: Houston Gaines (R, state Rep., Athens, Trump-endorsed) vs. Pamela DeLancy (D, retired Army nurse colonel, Henry County). District rated Solid/Safe R (Cook PVI R+11). CONFLICT UPDATE: SB 3EX (signed by Gov. Kemp on June 25, 2026 during the special session) delays the SB 189 QR-code tabulation ban to Jan 1, 2028. GA-10 counties will use existing touchscreen ballot-marking devices with QR-code tabulation for Nov 3, 2026. SB 3EX also mandates automatic hand recounts (< 0.5% margin) for the top-2 statewide races — not the U.S. House. One conflict remains unresolved: state certification deadline (Nov 20 by statute vs. commonly assumed Nov 17). GA-10-specific issue: Oconee County has an active SEB complaint referred to the Georgia AG in Feb 2026 over candidate-qualifying-date practices, and separately ran the June 2026 runoff with only 5 days of early voting at a single site. Drop-box availability could not be confirmed for Elbert, Franklin, Hart, Taliaferro, and Wilkes counties. All 26 sources verified as of July 20, 2026.
